transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m here because my sleep has gotten really unreliable. Even when I’m exhausted and get into bed, I end up lying there thinking through sales forecasts and team problems. Then I’ll wake up at like 3 or 4 in the morning and my brain just won’t shut off again.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about many different things during the day?

Yes, most days. My mind just jumps from one thing to the next—whether we’re going to hit the launch numbers, whether someone on my team might quit, then the mortgage, or a client renewal. It feels like even a small delay could turn into something major.
How long have you been worrying like this most days?
It’s been going on most days for about thirteen months now. It really started building after the sales division reorganization.
When you start worrying, do you find it hard to stop or control the worrying?

Yes. I’ll tell myself, like, “Brenda, you already made the plan, just let it go,” and I mean it in the moment. But then a few minutes later I’m right back in it. I’ll settle one concern in my head and then three more come up. It’s hard to shut it down.
Do you often notice your muscles feeling tense or tight?

Yes. I feel wound up almost all the time, and my shoulders are usually tight. Even if I’m just at home eating dinner, it can feel like I’m sitting in a tense work meeting, and I can’t really get my body to relax.
Do you often have trouble concentrating because your mind feels preoccupied with worry?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I do get distracted sometimes, but I haven’t paid close attention to whether it’s because I’m worrying or just because there’s a lot going on.
Have you been more irritable than usual?

Yes, I have. I’ve been snapping at my reps over small things, like minor CRM updates, and then at home I’ll get irritated with my husband over dishes in the sink. Afterward I usually realize my reaction was bigger than the situation.
Have you been feeling easily fatigued or worn out?
I’m not sure. I mean, I get tired like anyone does, especially after work, but I haven’t really noticed feeling unusually worn out in a way that stands out.
Do you often feel restless or keyed up, like you can’t really settle down?

Yes. I feel wound up a lot of the time, honestly. Even when I’m just at home eating dinner, it can feel like I’m still sitting in a pipeline review or waiting for something to go wrong. My shoulders stay tight, and it’s hard to really settle down even when I’m trying to relax.
Have you been feeling down or depressed?
I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve been stressed and on edge, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling depressed or down most of the time.
Have these worries and sleep problems been interfering with how well you function at work or at home?

Yes, it has. At work I spend so much time second-guessing decisions that meetings, especially pipeline reviews, get really tense. And then when I get home, I’m just drained and kind of reactive, so I’m not as present with my husband as I want to be.
